lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The overhaul is no longer theory - it's camp reality now, and that's where the Leafs will be judged. John Chayka's admission that a Morgan Rielly trade never came close leaves Toronto with its longtime defenseman still in the fold, while Auston Matthews is back in the picture talking like a man who expects this thing to work. The club finished 2025-26 at the bottom of the scoreboard in the only way that matters - the season is over - and now the focus shifts to whether this reshaped roster can actually breathe. Matthews' health, Easton Cowan's push for top-six duty, and the look of the blue line will tell the story. Training camp will answer whether the new-look Leafs are sturdier or just busier.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The drumbeat out of Toronto is not about summer glory anymore - it's about repair work. The Blue Jays' pitching woes were exposed in a costly series loss to Detroit, and the damage lands hard in a season that ends with the club at 74-88. The rotation has been patched together, and the numbers tell the tale: 21 percent of their innings came from pitchers drafted or developed in-house, a welcome sign in a year that chewed through arms. Shane Bieber and Anthony Santander are both pushing through recovery work, while Trey Yesavage's rehab track gives the front office one more reason to look hard at its depth chart. What matters now is whether Toronto turns that pipeline progress into a sturdier staff before spring training opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The summer silence broke with a thud - Kawhi Leonard's return to Toronto is finally official - and that changes the whole temperature around this franchise. The Raptors are in the deep offseason, but this is no sleepy holding pattern; it's a roster built around a 35-year-old star who still drags gravity with him, and the club's record last season is now just backdrop, not excuse. Leonard's arrival gives Toronto a headline and a hinge point, while the front office has already paid the price in Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and a pile of draft capital. Now the job is simpler and harder: make the fit work. Training camp will tell whether this is a splash or a structure.

the_latest.headline: Raptors, Leonard turn attention to basketball with trade now complete

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The offseason has already turned sharp-edged, and Washington is making the kind of practical, unsentimental moves that keep a roster from fraying at the seams. Veteran guard Lucas Patrick is coming aboard - a clear signal the line needed sturdier hands after the latest shuffle - and that matters more than any spring sermon. Frankie Luvu's groin strain only sharpens the point: this team cannot afford soft spots when the calendar flips toward camp. The Commanders finished last season 12-5, and that record now serves as a warning label, not a badge; good teams get scouted, patched, and pushed. Patrick brings experience. Luvu brings urgency. What to watch next is whether Washington can turn these stopgaps into a cleaner, tougher front before camp opens.

article.title: Wednesday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs open camp with a fresh look and a big question: whether the overhaul can actually settle the roster, while a separate report says the long-rumored Morgan Rielly trade never got off the ground. In Toronto baseball, the Blue Jays are still working through pitching trouble after a costly series loss to the Tigers.

For the Raptors, the focus has shifted to fit and timing now that the Kawhi deal is complete, with training camp conversation centered on how the pieces will mesh. In Washington, the Commanders are under the microscope after the Lucas Patrick signing, and the next clear checkpoint is Week 2 at Dallas, where the matchup with the Cowboys will draw a hard look.
